newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Unity government seen in Angola by year-end.
newsitem.headline: Unity government seen in Angola by year-end.

text.p: A number of UNITA generals will be sworn into the Angolan army on Tuesday and a national unity government is expected to be formed in Angola before the end of the year, Portuguese Foreign Minister Jaime Gama said on Monday.

"We underline the good news...that UNITA generals will be sworn into the Angolan national army tomorrow and that by the end of the year there will be the formation of a government of national unity," Gama told a news conference after meeting visiting Angolan Foreign Minister Venancio de Moura.
De Moura said: "By tomorrow the generals will be sworn in."
He added: "We are hoping soon for some appointments in the political area...for the national unity government -- this month we hope."
U.N. peacekeepers in Angola said on Saturday that the 20-year-old UNITA rebel army had practically disbanded as required by a peace plan, opening the way for a united country.
UNITA agreed in a 1994 accord with the Marxist government it had fought for two decades to dismantle its army gradually and merge some of its soldiers into a new, united Angolan force.
Nine UNITA generals have already been absorbed into the national army.
The United Nations has urged UNITA leader Jonas Savimbi and Angolan President Jose Eduardo dos Santos to meet inside Angola soon to establish a government of national unity and reconciliation.
Recent attempts to arrange a summit between the two men have failed, despite intervention by South African president Nelson Mandela and other leaders in the region.
